data_sources.name: FDA reclassification events (Federal Register records, 1980-2015; Class III to II and Class II to I; plus 2015 and late-2019 events)
FDA PMA and 510(k) databases (device submissions, firm names, brand names, dates)
FDA MAUDE adverse event reports (1992-2019, about 9.2 million reports)
Dimensions patent grants extract (USPTO patents, 1976-2019, over 1.2 million medical device patents)
Kogan et al. (2017) patent market values (patent value in 2019 dollars, linked to firm assets)
CRSP/Compustat (firm asset totals for public firms)
Truven Health MarketScan commercial claims (1996-2013, outpatient paid amounts by HCPCS/CPT)
Nexis Uni (medical device tort, preemption and bankruptcy case counts)
Kelly and Seru (2021) patent novelty/breakthrough index
Makower et al. (2010) survey of FDA-related costs and delays (204 firms)
GPT-5-mini device-to-procedure concordance and GPT-4o device/not-device patent screening and device introduction year coding (constructed data)

data_processing_steps.description: Compile all FDA reclassification events from 1980-2015. Main Class III to II sample is the 12 FDA-initiated events (of 29; 17 were petition-driven and are excluded from the main sample). Device types need at least one PMA submission or patent before reclassification. Class II to I events (1996/1998 events) need at least one pre-event patent. Later-treated controls are Class III to II events after 2015 (outcomes censored after 2015) and Class II to I devices moved in late 2019.

Build device-type-year counts from the FDA PMA/510(k) data using fuzzy firm-name matching: new entry (firm's first-ever submission), incumbent entry (firm with prior submissions starting in a new device type), and unique device submissions (first occurrence of a brand name within a type). Regulatory proficiency is the firm's cumulative approval delay in days up to each submission.
variables_involved: cumulative approval days / cumulative product count

data_processing_steps.description: Construct device-type-year serious adverse event counts from MAUDE (deaths, hospitalizations, life-threatening events, disabilities). Also build severity share (serious events divided by total reports) and events per linked procedure (for 15 deregulated device types, using MarketScan volumes). Link the 300 largest reporting manufacturers to CRSP/Compustat assets (88 are private with no match).

Link patents to over 5,000 FDA device types by keyword search (all keywords from regulation-number and device-name descriptions must appear in the patent text) in Dimensions. A patent matched to several types is randomly assigned to one. Aggregate by initial filing date to device-type-year patent counts. Robustness samples: CPC A61* excluding A61P, and a GPT-4o device/not-device screen.

Patent quality: forward citations (excluding examiner citations) and Kogan et al. market value (2019 dollars, public firms only). Zeros are assigned when no patents are filed in a device-type-year. Safety emphasis is a binary device-type-year indicator equal to one if any patent title or abstract contains a safety term from a Word2Vec-selected keyword list. Breakthrough patents use the Kelly-Seru novelty index.

Price data: GPT-5-mini links FDA product codes to outpatient CPT/HCPCS procedures (15 Class II to I types; 3 of 12 Class III to II types). Compare with an expert-coder concordance. Aggregate MarketScan paid amounts to annual mean paid amounts by linked device type. Controls are CPTs matched on pre-event mean price from the full CPT universe, or procedures tied to device-type controls. Sample is about 17,400 procedure codes and 182,200 procedure-year observations.

Build three control groups: later-treated, intuitive (similar ailment and risk), and matched. Matched controls are the two nearest never-reclassified product codes using 5-year pre-event means. Adverse events use Mahalanobis distance; innovation and market structure use squared Euclidean distance on patent counts and new firms patenting (plus device submissions for III to II); patent quality uses forward citations and real patent value. Matched units must have at least one pre-period patent, and device types treating the same indications as the treated code are excluded.

Stacked difference-in-differences (Cengiz et al. 2019). Panels are event-specific, with event-by-device-type and event-by-year fixed effects. The reclass indicator turns on at announcement for forward-looking outcomes (patents) and at enactment for FDA-derived outcomes. Inference uses Conley-Taber for small numbers of treated events. Estimated separately for Class III to II and Class II to I. Robustness: Borusyak et al. imputation, log(y+1), quasi-Poisson, and dropping zero-count device types.

Heterogeneity analysis: DiD by tercile of firm regulatory proficiency (device submissions) and by tercile of firm assets (patenting rate, probability of any safety innovation, probability of any serious event, using an LPM at the firm-within-device-type level).

Market age and device-level analysis: market age is the reclassification year minus the earliest of first clinical study, earliest patent, or first FDA submission, using hand coding plus GPT-4o (r=0.76 against hand-coded values for 25 down-regulated types). Device-level DiD effects on severity share and patents are regressed on market age with controls for baseline severity, baseline patenting, device-category FE, and an FDA-initiated indicator (III to II) or the Device Priority Model score (II to I). A back-of-the-envelope cost-benefit calculation follows.

Proxy Device Priority Model score: 0.38*Deaths + 0.30*Serious Injuries + 0.12*Less-Serious Injuries (average annual adverse-event counts). LDA topic modeling of patent titles and abstracts, with the topic count chosen by coherence, gives topic-device-year panels for product variety.
